title: Argon's Pricing Cliff, Ecosia Leaves Mistral
summary: Google's Gemini 4 Argon is now broadly available, but its introductory API price doubles on December first. Also: Mistral Large 4 in preview, Ecosia's switch from Mistral to open models on European servers, new evidence that LLM judges are over-trusted, and the December second AI Act marking deadline.
headlines: Ecosia leaves Mistral for open models
AI Act marking deadline December second

story_of_the_day.facts: Google made Gemini 4 Argon broadly available on October thirteenth. It had announced the model on September thirtieth, with access limited to a cyber defender programme. It is now on the paid Gemini API and in AI Studio, with no free tier. The model ID is gemini-4-argon, with a one-million-token context window. Introductory pricing is two dollars per million input tokens and ten dollars per million output tokens, and output includes thinking tokens. Cached input costs ten cents per million tokens. That introductory rate runs through November thirtieth. From December first, every rate doubles: four dollars per million input tokens, twenty dollars per million output tokens, and twenty cents per million cached tokens.
story_of_the_day.read: The read here: the doubling is a budget event, not a footnote. A team that benchmarks Argon now and builds its business case on the introductory rate will find that case half wrong in December. Rerun your cost-per-task estimates at four dollars and twenty dollars. Make sure your gateway reports spend by model and by use case, so the cliff is visible before the invoice. And keep a cheaper fallback route warm for tasks that do not need long reasoning, since thinking tokens are billed as output. It is also worth checking the expiry dates on any other promotional rates in your catalogue.
story_of_the_day.label: confirmed

segments.facts: Mistral Large 4 entered public preview on the Mistral API on October sixth. It is a mixture-of-experts model of about one trillion parameters with a one-million-token context. List price is one dollar thirty-six per million input tokens and four dollars eighteen per million output tokens. A fifty percent launch discount was set for two weeks from October sixth. Open weights are promised by the end of October, licence not yet named.
segments.read: Why it matters: a preview is not a production commitment, and no general availability date has been given. Treat it as a candidate for your evaluation set, not a routing default. The licence will decide whether private or on-premise deployment is possible, so it is worth watching.

segments.facts: Berlin search engine Ecosia switched from OpenAI to Mistral in May, and has now dropped Mistral, according to Politico's reporting this month. Its CEO cited quality, overloaded capacity and cost, and says costs roughly halved. It now runs open models, including Chinese ones, via Melious, a German platform hosting them on servers in eight EU countries.
segments.read: What this really signals: sovereignty is being unbundled. Where a model runs and whether its weights are open can be separate procurement criteria, so a European host for open weights now competes with a European model vendor. One customer's claim is not a benchmark, so run your own evaluation.

segments.facts: A Kili Technology analysis published October sixteenth summarises two 2026 preprints. One ran twenty-one LLM judges through about 541000 judgments, and found that raw agreement metrics overstated quality. The other audited annotator pools: expert and crowd labellers split on 23.6 percent of items each pool had called unanimous.
segments.read: The bigger picture: percent agreement with humans is what many judge setups report, and it flatters them. Use chance-corrected agreement, and audit who produced your reference labels. This is a vendor's summary of preprints, so read the studies before changing your method.
segments.label: confirmed

sources.title: Kili Technology: LLM-as-a-Judge Validity: What 541,000 Decisions Reveal

segments.facts: The Digital Omnibus on AI has been in force since July twenty-seventh. It moved stand-alone high-risk obligations to December second, 2027, and embedded-product ones to August second, 2028. Article 50 transparency duties applied from August second, 2026. Generative systems already on the market have until December second, 2026 to mark outputs in machine-readable form.
segments.read: Why it matters: the high-risk reprieve gets the headlines, but the nearer date is December second. Check whether you are a provider or a deployer for each generative feature, and whether your vendors pass provenance marking through your gateway. Legal should confirm the roles.

number_of_the_day.text: 33 to 41 points: how much raw agreement overstated LLM-judge quality on MT-Bench once chance agreement was removed, across twenty-one judges. Your judge's headline score may be a lot weaker than it looks.

what_to_watch: This week, Mistral Large 4's two-week launch discount, counted from October sixth, should lapse, so list prices are likely to apply. Open weights are promised by the end of October, and sources differ on the exact day. On Saturday, October twenty-fourth, AWS runs its European Sovereign Cloud independence exercise. Further out: Vertex AI Extensions shuts down after November twenty-sixth, Argon's introductory price ends November thirtieth, and AI Act marking applies December second.
question: If Gemini 4 Argon's price doubles on December first, which of your workloads break their budget, and does your gateway already show spend by model and by team?
